coverage: Targeted diagram review of the product basis of M⊗_R N at statement lines 30–41 and its proof, checking the I×J indexing, canonical map, finite support, balancing, and empty-basis cases.

findings.evidence: The source identifies M with ⊕_{i∈I}R and N with ⊕_{j∈J}R. Tensoring these direct sums and using R⊗_R R≅R gives M⊗_R N≅⊕_{(i,j)∈I×J}R. The canonical map φ:R^(I×J)→M⊗_R N sends the coordinate vector at (i,j) to e_i⊗f_j, so the indexed family is exactly the product-indexed basis.

R^(I×J) means finitely supported coefficient families on I×J. For m=Σ_i a_i e_i and n=Σ_j b_j f_j, both sums are finite and m⊗n=Σ_(i,j) a_i b_j(e_i⊗f_j), a finite sum. The coordinate pairing (m,n)↦(a_i b_j)_(i,j) is R-bilinear because R is commutative, hence induces a map out of M⊗_R N; it is inverse to φ on elementary basis tensors. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, while uniqueness follows from the direct-sum isomorphism. The proof's direct-sum route establishes the same claim.
If I or J is empty, the corresponding free module is zero and I×J is empty. Thus R^(I×J)=0 and M⊗_R N=0, so φ is the unique isomorphism between zero modules, as the source states.

findings.check: Module actions, naturality, and coset indexing
findings.evidence: This is a tensor product of modules over the same commutative ring R; no additional left/right action conventions, cosets, or double cosets occur. The theorem claims a canonical isomorphism relative to the chosen bases and makes no separate naturality claim.

A small schematic could show a generic pair (i,j) indexing e_i⊗f_j and the map from the free module on I×J. It should not depict I and J as necessarily finite or represent R^(I×J) as unrestricted coefficient arrays. The source already states the map, finite expansion, and empty case explicitly, so a diagram is optional.
